# Appendix A — The Plackett–Luce objective in torch {#sec-appx-a}

Paper 3 implements the depth-$k$ Plackett–Luce likelihood as a custom
XGBoost objective with an analytic gradient. This paper needs the same
likelihood as a differentiable loss over variable-length races. It is
verified against paper 3's implementation rather than trusted.

## Verification against paper 3

`scripts/verify_p5_pl_torch.R` asserts agreement with the function paper 3
was fitted with, on identical inputs: random scores at mixed field sizes;
the edge cases, meaning two-runner races, races at exactly $k+1$ runners,
and ragged and single-race batches; depths $k = 1$ to 4; shift invariance;
and score vectors spread widely enough that a naive `exp()` overflows.

Agreement is about 1e-9 relative. The gradient matches finite differences to
2.9e-8, and matches paper 3's analytic gradient to 2.9e-8, so this paper
descends the same surface paper 3 did. The check was run in two fresh R
processes rather than twice within one, since state held at the process
level can make a broken setting look verified on a second call.

## The two-optimiser check

Agreement on a loss value does not establish that an optimiser reaches the
same place. A linear scorer was therefore fitted in torch on paper 2b's
seventeen features and its validation loss compared with paper 2b's own
`{mlogit}` fit on the same rows — gradient descent against iteratively
reweighted least squares, on the same objective and the same data.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-two-optim
#| tbl-cap: "Two optimisers on the same objective and the same 17 features, validation Plackett–Luce loss per race."
tibble::tibble(
  Fit = c("paper 2b, `{mlogit}`, closed form",
          "linear scorer, torch, Adam"),
  `Val PL loss` = c(fmt_loss(loss_2b),
                    fmt_loss(p5_diag_linear$best_val_pl_loss)),
  `Best epoch` = c("—", as.character(p5_diag_linear$best_epoch))
) |>
  kable(align = "lrr")
```

The two agree to
`r formatC(abs(loss_2b - p5_diag_linear$best_val_pl_loss), format = "e", digits = 1)`
per race, with the torch fit marginally the lower — which is what a
first-order method run to convergence should produce against a closed-form
fit with a different convergence tolerance.

## A bug a check on the loss value would have passed

Entries that pad a race out to a common width must not contribute to its
denominator. Writing that condition as `torch_where(mask, value, fallback)`
returns the value of one branch but computes derivatives for both, and the
discarded branch here contained $\log 0$.

The forward loss was therefore exactly correct — agreeing with paper 3's
implementation to 1e-9 — while the gradient was `NaN`. A check on the loss
value alone would have passed it and left every fit broken. The fix makes
the denominator finite before the condition is applied rather than relying
on the condition to remove an infinity, and the gate now asserts a finite
gradient as well as a correct value.
